title: The first 100 wallets make the network
dek: Network El Segundo opens a free, public Tezos roll call — one Kukai signature, one verified wallet, one invitation to pass on
body:
Network El Segundo is looking for its first one hundred Tezos wallets. Joining costs nothing: open the release through PointCast, connect with Kukai, and sign one wallet-control message. The signature does not buy art, mint a token, move tez, or approve a transaction. It proves one thing only — that one person controls one Tezos Mainnet address — and the deduplicated public counter moves by one.

The founding rule is simple: bring one wallet, then pass the same clean link to one Tezos artist, collector, builder, or curious friend. PointCast publishes the count, the press filing, the house-campaign receipt, and the machine-readable release packet so the milestone can be checked instead of merely announced.

The future commerce idea remains a prototype. A qualifying art purchase would add its wallet to a distribution list, with 50 percent of each recorded sale reserved for eligible participants after that sale. No live sale contract, payout contract, token, automated yield system, investment, or return is part of this roll call. First the people; then the system; proof at every step.
